article.headline: Snowflake Dips 2.4% After Hours; Sales Climb 35.1% On AI Data Cloud
article.deck: The eight-week cup's buy point is 384.66, 11.6% above the close; the stock bounced off its 50-day line today, and the handle high at 348.38 is the early entry.
body: Snowflake traded at 331.74 after hours, down 8.17, or 2.4%, as of 5:35 p.m. ET, as software names on the desk's list sold off late after ServiceNow and Fortinet reported. Snowflake has no report out. In the regular session it rose 2.49, or 0.7%, to 339.91 on volume 0.56x its 50-day average, after the day's low touched the 50-day line at 332.22 and the stock closed above it. The after-hours price sits just under that line.

Snowflake sells a cloud data platform. Companies pull their data into one place, build applications on it, share it with partners and run AI against it. Its customers span financial services, advertising and media, retail and consumer goods, healthcare, manufacturing, technology, telecom and travel. A Wednesday headline said Snowflake became a native AI Data Cloud service on a major cloud platform.

Revenue is the story. Sales in the fiscal second quarter, ended July 31, rose 35.1% to $1.55 billion, and revenue climbed in each of the four quarters in the table: $1.21 billion, $1.28 billion, $1.39 billion and $1.55 billion. The company still loses money, but the loss narrowed to 0.55 a share from 0.86 the quarter before, after losses of 0.87 and 0.90 in the two quarters prior.

The market values Snowflake at $119.92 billion, and the stock trades at 112.3 times forward earnings, a price set on the sales line, not on profits. Shares are up 55.0% this year and 27.8% over 12 months. RS rank is 92 of 99 on the desk's list, with the RS line 7.1% under its high.

The chart is an eight-week cup, 21.4% deep, with the rim on Sept. 3 and the low of 302.24 on Oct. 16. The buy point is 384.66, a dime over the 52-week high of 384.56, and the buy range runs to 403.89; the close is 11.6% below the buy point. The stock is 0.18 ATRs from its 21-day line at 332.36, and the 21-day and 50-day lines sit together near 332.

Two earlier entries are live on the desk's list. The handle high of 348.38 from Sept. 30 is 2.4% above the close; clearing it is the early entry. The second is today's 50-day bounce: the entry is above today's high, and the line is the stop. A close back under the 50-day line, where the after-hours price already sits, would cancel the bounce.
Next earnings are due Dec. 2.
article.watch: Whether Snowflake opens above its 50-day line at 332.22; the handle high at 348.38 is the next level above.

article.headline: Visa Says U.S. Consumer Isn't Cracking; Shares Ease 0.3% After Earnings
article.deck: The close is 3.9% above the six-week flat base's 385.67 buy point and inside the buy range to 404.95.
body: Visa fell 1.26, or 0.3%, to 400.60 after its fiscal fourth-quarter report, on volume 1.14x its 50-day average, and traded at 401.50 after hours, up 0.2%. The stock broke out Oct. 12, 12 sessions ago, from a six-week flat base, 7.5% deep, with a buy point of 385.67 and a buy range to 404.95; the breakout session traded 0.80x average. The close sits 3.9% above the buy point.

Visa is 3.4% off its 52-week high of 414.60, 5.6% above its 50-day line at 379.45 and 1.8% above its 21-day line at 393.53, 0.07 ATRs from the 21-day line, the session's low holding just above it. RS rank is 70 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 4.3% under its high. Shares are up 14.2% this year and 15.2% over 12 months.

The latest quarter in the desk's table, ended June 30, showed EPS up 10.4% to 2.97 a share on revenue of $11.63 billion, up 14.4%; the fiscal fourth-quarter figures are not in the table yet. Revenue rose in each of the four quarters listed, from $10.72 billion. Forward P/E is 23.4 on a market value of $752.07 billion. The next report is due Jan. 26.

Headlines said Visa reported fiscal fourth-quarter results, said the U.S. consumer isn't cracking, and laid out its fiscal 2027 outlook and growth priorities on the call. IBD named it Stock of the Day for bullish action after the report.
A close under the 21-day line at 393.53 would be the first crack in the move.
article.watch: Whether Visa holds the 21-day line at 393.53 and stays inside the range below 404.95.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7743.98 and sits 0.6% above its 50-day line; the Nasdaq gained 0.3% to 26549.85 but remains 0.1% below its 50-day, and the Dow added 0.2% to 52475.10, 0.4% above its 50-day. The S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions and the Nasdaq and Dow 3 each, and the desk's state is Uptrend under pressure. After the close the selling hit software: Fortinet fell 24.6% and ServiceNow 18.1% on earnings, Alphabet dropped 10.6%, Sprouts Farmers Market 20.6% and Marvell 8.7%, with Palo Alto Networks, Rubrik, Zscaler, Salesforce and Atlassian each down 6.2% to 6.7%, while Carvana rose 8.2%, Chipotle 6.6% and TJX 6.5%. Leadership is thin: Amgen, ServiceNow and Tesla are the week's breakouts still above their buy points at the close, Eli Lilly and Apple are back testing theirs, and AI chips (average RS 74), software (69) and energy (67) lead the groups, with ExxonMobil and EOG Resources sitting in buy ranges.

chief.verdict: The leaders cracked after the bell, and it was software that cracked: FTNT fell 24.6% to 131.28, NOW fell 18.1% to 123.0, and GTLB fell 6.2% to 54.40 in after-hours trade, all of them buy-range names an hour earlier. What still holds up is slow money: Visa with its earnings behind it, and oil and drug names that trade on earnings dates instead of a chart. Several breakouts this week came on below-average volume (V 0.8, EOG 0.82, GTLB 0.87, NOW 0.95 times normal), so institutions are not pushing these names, and the risk leans lower.
chief.market: With the Big Picture at Uptrend under pressure, S&P 500 distribution days at 5, Nasdaq at 3 and the Nasdaq 0.1% below its 50-day line, keep exposure light: one or two new positions at most, sized small.

picks.why: The cleanest chart on the list: a 6-week flat base only 7.5% deep, the close at 400.6 just 1.8% above the 21-day line, and the next earnings report not until 2027-01-26, so there is no report to gap through. The risk is the breakout itself, which came on volume only 0.8 times normal with RS at 70; this is a slow steady name, not a leader that will double.
picks.entry: Buy only between the 385.67 buy point and the 404.95 top of the range, on a session that closes up with volume above its 50-day average; cut it on a close back under 385.67.

The risk is the software selloff: it traded at 32.50 after hours, back under the 32.91 buy point.

After hours it traded at 331.74, under the 332.22 50-day line, so the bounce has not held yet, and the cup is 21.4% deep.
picks.entry: Do not start before the 384.66 buy point unless it reclaims 332.22 and then clears the 348.38 handle high on volume above average; the 50-day line is the stop.

The breakout came on volume only 0.95 times normal with the RS line 29.6% off its high, and the earnings miss sent it to 123.0 after hours, well under the 149.7 buy point.

At 404.22 it sits 4.5% above the 386.93 buy point, near the 406.28 top of the range, with RS at 66, the RS line 27.5% off its high and the latest quarter's EPS down 43.6%: late in the range on a weak RS line.
